q: How long is the Juan Bautista de Anza Trail in Moreno Valley?
a: The Moreno Valley segment is approximately 8 miles long, running diagonally north-to-south across the city from Towngate Boulevard to the Lake Perris State Recreation Area.

q: What is the trail surface and width?
a: The trail is fully paved (asphalt and Portland cement concrete, built with recycled materials), flat, and ADA-compliant with ramps at intersections. It sits on a 100-foot-wide California DWR water pipeline easement.

q: Where can I access the trail in Moreno Valley?
a: The trail runs from Towngate Boulevard in the north, through the Moreno Valley Mall area and Iris Avenue, past El Potrero Park, and south to the Lake Perris State Recreation Area. The July 2024 NPS dedication ceremony was held at John F. Kennedy Veterans Memorial Park, 15115 Indian Street, a key access point.

q: Are bikes, dogs, horses, and wheelchairs allowed?
a: Yes — pedestrians, bicyclists, and equestrians are all permitted. Dogs must be leashed at all times and waste picked up. The trail is ADA-compliant with ramps, making it wheelchair- and stroller-accessible. Bicyclists must yield to pedestrians and equestrians; motorized vehicles are not allowed.

q: What does the name "Juan Bautista de Anza" refer to?
a: The trail honors Juan Bautista de Anza, an 18th-century Spanish military commander who led the 1775-76 overland expedition from Sonora, Mexico to San Francisco, establishing one of the first non-native settlements in California. The 1,200-mile Juan Bautista de Anza National Historic Trail, administered by the National Park Service, follows that route; Moreno Valley sits along it.

q: Does the trail connect to other parks or trails?
a: Yes. It is a certified segment of the 1,200-mile Juan Bautista de Anza National Historic Trail, which continues south into the Lake Perris State Recreation Area (CA State Parks) and links to the larger regional historic trail network. Within Moreno Valley it passes near nine parks and at least four schools.

q: Is the trail lit at night and are there mile markers?
a: Energy-saving LED safety lighting is included in the trail's design. The City has not published official mile-marker details; historical/interpretive signage tied to the Anza expedition was added as part of the 2024 NPS certification.
